summary: The Amalfi Coast is a stunning stretch of southern Italian coastline renowned for its dramatic cliffs, colorful villages, and world-class Mediterranean cuisine. Perched villages like Positano and Ravello offer breathtaking views, winding terraces of lemon groves, and some of Italy's most photographed landscapes. This enchanting destination perfectly balances relaxation, culinary exploration, and adventure activities.

restaurants.name: Franco Pepe at Pepe in Grani
restaurants.description: A Michelin-starred restaurant in nearby Salerno offering innovative coastal cuisine with locally sourced ingredients. Chef Franco Pepe creates artistic dishes that blend tradition with modern techniques.
restaurants.mustTry: Pasta with sea urchin and bottarga

restaurants.name: La Gavitella
restaurants.description: Elegant hilltop restaurant in Praiano with panoramic views of the Tyrrhenian Sea. Specializes in fresh seafood and traditional Campanian dishes prepared with exceptional care.

restaurants.name: Da Adolfo
restaurants.description: A beachfront institution accessible only by water or steep stairs, this family-run trattoria serves incredibly fresh seafood in an intimate setting. Known for its simplicity and quality ingredients.

restaurants.name: Casa Costagliola
restaurants.description: Charming family restaurant in Positano offering traditional Amalfi Coast cuisine with reasonable prices. Famous for their homemade pasta and fresh seafood caught daily.

restaurants.name: Le Botteghe
restaurants.description: Intimate tavern-style eatery in Ravello featuring traditional Campanian mountain and coastal dishes. Intimate candlelit setting with excellent local wines.

restaurants.name: Pizzeria Vicolo
restaurants.description: Casual neighborhood pizzeria in Amalfi town serving authentic Neapolitan pizza at budget-friendly prices. Perfect for a quick, satisfying meal with locals.

restaurants.name: Il Pirata
restaurants.description: Waterfront restaurant in Positano with colorful decor and stunning sea views. Known for fresh pasta, seafood risotto, and an excellent wine selection.

restaurants.name: Trattoria del Capo
restaurants.description: Family-owned restaurant in Atrani featuring simple, authentic coastal cuisine using centuries-old recipes. Minimal fuss, maximum flavor with daily specials.
restaurants.mustTry: Pasta e patate (pasta and potato soup)

restaurants.name: Ristorante Rossellinis
restaurants.description: Michelin-starred restaurant in Ravello with breathtaking garden views and innovative Mediterranean cuisine. Chef Crescenzo Scappaticci creates visual and culinary masterpieces.

restaurants.name: O'Canonico
restaurants.description: Cozy restaurant in Positano specializing in fresh pasta made daily and locally caught fish. Warm atmosphere with personalized service from the owner.

restaurants.name: Pasticceria Sal De Riso
restaurants.description: Famous pastry shop and café throughout the coast serving exceptional desserts, pastries, and gelato. Perfect for breakfast or afternoon treats.

restaurants.name: Maria Grazia
restaurants.description: Unassuming beachfront restaurant in Praiano serving the freshest seafood with minimal preparation. Tables literally on the sand with direct sea access.

activities.name: Positano Village Exploration
activities.description: Wander through the vertical village of Positano, discovering steep winding streets, pastel buildings, boutiques, and artwork. Stop at viewpoints and small cafés to soak in the ambiance.

activities.name: Boat Tour Along the Coast
activities.description: Experience the coastline from the water with visits to hidden coves, sea caves, and pristine beaches accessible only by boat. Many tours include swimming and snorkeling opportunities.

activities.name: Hiking the Path of Gods
activities.description: Trek the famous Sentiero degli Dei trail between Praiano and Positano, offering panoramic views of the coastline and Mediterranean Sea. Moderate difficulty with stunning photo opportunities throughout.

activities.name: Ravello Town & Villa Visits
activities.description: Explore the hilltop town of Ravello with its stunning villas like Villa d'Este and Villa Rufolo, featuring beautiful gardens and coastal views. Visit the cathedral and local artisan shops.

activities.name: Lemon Grove Tour
activities.description: Visit a family-run lemon grove terraced into the cliffs, learning about cultivation of lemons used for limoncello and local cuisine. Includes tastings and samples of local products.

activities.name: Amalfi Town Historic Walk
activities.description: Discover the main town's maritime history, stunning cathedral with Arab-Norman architecture, and ancient trading heritage. Browse local shops, museums, and waterfront areas.

activities.name: Scuba Diving & Snorkeling
activities.description: Explore vibrant underwater ecosystems with multiple dive sites featuring colorful fish, underwater caves, and reefs. Suitable for beginners to advanced divers with certified guides.

activities.name: Cooking Class at Local Home
activities.description: Learn to prepare authentic Amalfi Coast cuisine in a local family kitchen or cooking school, including pasta making, seafood preparation, and traditional recipes. Includes a multi-course meal.

activities.name: Limoncello & Wine Tasting
activities.description: Visit local producers to taste authentic limoncello, local wines, and other regional specialties while learning about production methods. Many locations offer beautiful terrace settings.

activities.name: Beach Day at Spiaggia Grande
activities.description: Spend a day at Positano's main beach with its pebbles, crystal-clear water, and beachfront restaurants. Rent beach umbrellas and enjoy swimming, sunbathing, and people-watching.

activities.name: Atrani Village Discovery
activities.description: Visit the smallest municipality in Italy, a charming fishing village with authentic local character, minimal tourism, and stunning harbor views. Perfect for photography and peaceful exploration.

activities.name: Sunset Aperitivo Experience
activities.description: Enjoy evening drinks and appetizers at a clifftop bar or beachfront establishment while watching the sun set over the Tyrrhenian Sea. Sample local wines and limoncello.

spots.name: Positano Main Beach Viewpoint
spots.description: Elevated view of the iconic vertical village cascading down to the sea with colorful buildings, boats, and Mediterranean waters.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour, early morning or sunset

spots.name: Praiano Terraces
spots.description: Dramatic clifftop terraces with lemon groves overlooking the coast, perfect for wide-angle landscape shots.
spots.bestTime: Morning light for detail, evening for backlighting

spots.name: Amalfi Cathedral Facade
spots.description: Stunning Arab-Norman architecture of the white and black striped cathedral with intricate bronze doors and historic details.

spots.name: Path of Gods Trail Overlook
spots.description: Breathtaking panoramic views of the coastline, villages, and sea accessible from the hiking trail with multiple vantage points.
spots.bestTime: Mid-morning or late afternoon for light direction

spots.name: Ravello Villa d'Este Gardens
spots.description: Manicured terraced gardens with stone sculptures, Mediterranean plants, and dramatic sea views through cypress trees.
spots.bestTime: Morning light in gardens, sunset for broader vistas

spots.name: Atrani Harbor
spots.description: Authentic fishing village harbor with colorful boats, weathered buildings, and locals, offering authentic street photography.
spots.bestTime: Early morning when fishermen work, golden hour

spots.name: Emerald Grotto Cave Interior
spots.description: Ethereal water cave with bioluminescent green hues reflected in still water, accessed by boat.

spots.name: Lemon Grove Terraces at Sunset
spots.description: Yellow lemon fruits against green foliage with Mediterranean sea in background, bathed in warm evening light.

spots.name: Conca dei Marini Beach
spots.description: Small secluded beach with turquoise water, fishing boats, and dramatic cliff backdrop creating composition depth.
spots.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon for side lighting

spots.name: Furore Fjord
spots.description: Hidden fjord with emerald waters surrounded by steep cliffs and small village, accessible by steep stairs.
spots.bestTime: Midday for water color, late afternoon for cliff lighting

lensRecommendations: 16-35mm wide-angle for expansive landscape and village architecture shots
50mm prime for intimate street photography and architectural details in villages
70-200mm telephoto for compressed perspective of coastal layers and distant vistas
Macro lens for detail shots of lemons, local crafts, and food photography
photography.goldenHourNotes: The Amalfi Coast experiences exceptional golden hour light due to its east-west cliff orientation, with the western sea providing dramatic backlighting in late afternoon. Evening light transforms the pastel villages into warm, saturated colors, while morning light illuminates terraces and creates long shadows. Plan shoots during the 1-2 hours before sunset for optimal warm tones and landscape depth.

weather.seasonality: Summer (July-August) is peak season with hot temperatures and crowded attractions, while spring (April-May) and fall (September-October) offer ideal weather with fewer tourists. Winter months are cool and rainy but provide a quieter, more authentic experience.
weather.summary: The Amalfi Coast enjoys a Mediterranean climate with warm, dry summers perfect for beach activities and cool, wet winters. Spring and fall are ideal visiting seasons with pleasant temperatures ranging from 16-24°C and manageable rainfall.

hotels.name: Hotel Positano
hotels.description: Simple family-run hotel in the heart of Positano offering comfortable rooms with basic amenities and proximity to the main beach and village attractions.

hotels.name: Hotel Ravello
hotels.description: Charming 3-star hotel with sea views, friendly staff, and convenient location for exploring Ravello's villas and cultural sites with a small pool.

hotels.name: Monastero Santa Rosa
hotels.description: Exclusive 5-star hotel built within a converted 17th-century monastery perched above the coast, offering spa services, fine dining, and private beach access with unparalleled views.
